Computerized Tomography (CT scan): An imaging test that combines a series of X-ray images taken from different angles to create detailed cross-sectional pictures of the bones, organs and soft tissues inside the body.
cubic centimeters (“cc’s”): A unit of volume equal to one milliliter, commonly used to measure doses of liquid medicine and fluids.
cystitis: Inflammation of the bladder, most often caused by a urinary tract infection.
dehydrated: Having lost more water and fluids than the body takes in, so it cannot carry out its normal functions.
Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA): The molecule that carries the genetic instructions for the growth, development and function of all living organisms.
diagnosis: The identification of a disease or condition by examining its signs, symptoms and test results.
dialysis: A treatment that filters waste, salt and extra water from the blood when the kidneys can no longer do it on their own.
dietitian: A health care professional who is an expert in food and nutrition and plans diets to promote health or manage disease.
digestive system: The group of organs, including the mouth, esophagus, stomach and intestines, that breaks food down into nutrients the body can absorb.
Dilation and Curettage (D & C): A procedure in which the cervix is widened (dilated) and tissue is scraped or suctioned from the lining of the uterus.
Diphtheria, Pertussis and Tetanus (DPT): A combination vaccine that protects against three serious bacterial infections: diphtheria, whooping cough (pertussis) and tetanus.
discharge (from hospital): The formal release of a patient from a hospital or other health care facility once inpatient care is no longer needed.
discharge instructions: The written directions a patient receives when leaving the hospital about medicines, activity, diet, wound care and follow-up visits.
discomfort: A mild feeling of pain, unease or physical distress.
distracted: Unable to concentrate or pay attention because the mind is drawn to something else.
diverticulitis: Inflammation or infection of small pouches (diverticula) that can form in the wall of the large intestine.
Do Not Resuscitate (DNR): A medical order telling health care providers not to perform CPR if a patient's breathing or heartbeat stops.
dosage: The amount of a medicine to be taken and how often to take it.
lice: Tiny wingless insects that live on the scalp or body, feed on human blood and cause itching.
Pregnancy: The period, usually about nine months, during which a baby develops inside a woman's uterus.
Prenatal Care: The medical checkups and health care a woman receives during pregnancy to protect her health and her baby's.
prescription: A written order from a licensed provider that authorizes a patient to receive a medicine or treatment.
procedure: A course of action performed to diagnose or treat a medical condition, such as a test or a surgery.
prognosis: The likely course and outcome of a disease, including the chances of recovery.
prostate (gland): A small gland in men, located below the bladder, that produces part of the fluid in semen.
radiology: The branch of medicine that uses imaging such as X-rays, CT, MRI and ultrasound to diagnose and treat disease.
Rapid eye movement (REM): A stage of sleep in which the eyes move quickly, brain activity increases and most dreaming occurs.
record: The file that documents a patient's medical history, diagnoses, treatments and test results.
recovered: Having returned to a normal state of health after an illness, injury or procedure.
recovery (room): The area of a hospital where patients are closely monitored as they wake up after surgery or anesthesia.
redness: A red color of the skin, often a sign of irritation, inflammation or infection.
referral: A request from one provider for a patient to see a specialist or receive a particular service.
refills: Additional supplies of a medicine authorized by the original prescription, so the patient can get more without a new one.
regular: Happening in a normal, steady pattern, such as a regular heartbeat or regular bowel movements.
release (from hospital): The formal discharge of a patient from a hospital or other health care facility.
respiration: The process of breathing: taking air into the lungs and letting it out.
seasonal allergies: Allergic reactions, such as sneezing and itchy eyes, to pollen or mold that appear during certain times of the year.
